source.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
source.summary: Investors have reacted to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry.
source.evidence_text:
Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in the US and Asia in a stock market rout after the US midterm elections sparked concerns of a slowdown in artificial intelligence development.
Democrats in races across the US campaigned to slow the growth of data centres and AI, and there were dozens of measures on ballots around the country aimed at restricting the development of the hubs crucial for powering the technology.
The sell-off comes on top of broader concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off.
The Nikkei 225 in Japan was 6% lower in early trading as shares in memory chip maker Kioxia lost over 12.6% and rival Tokyo Electron slipped by 9.5%.
The sell-off in Seoul sent the Kospi index plunging more than 8.5%, triggering a so-called circuit breaker, a mechanism that temporarily halts trading to curb panic selling.
They won both the US Senate and House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterms, taking control of Congress for the rest of President Donald Trump's presidency.
Texas' Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index closed down by more than 5.5%, losing an estimated $2.5tn (£1.9tn) in market value, according to Dow Jones data, while other key US stock indexes also saw big losses in their worst days since 2025.
Greater scrutiny of data centre approvals, and their impact on the environment and electricity bills could delay projects and raise costs across the industry, said Charu Chanana, Chief Investment Strategist at Saxo.
OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board.
The Nasdaq Composite fall was so large it is now in what market watchers call correction territory, which is where an index or company value falls at least 10% below its recent high.
"Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction."
While both political parties are keen to ensure the US' dominance in the technology, "there is a difference between supporting AI development and allowing infrastructure to expand at any cost or pace," she said.
Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks the performance of 30 of the largest companies involved in semiconductor production, fell by more than 12%.

vocabulary.definition: Made people worry that something bad might happen.
Worked to win public support for a plan during an election.
Delayed or paused for a period of time.
A measure that shows how the prices of a group of stocks change.
Finished the trading day at the level given.
A period when many investors sell their stocks, causing prices to drop sharply.
Bring enough financial benefit to make the money invested worthwhile.

grammar.explanation: Use “could” followed by the base form of a verb to describe a possible effect. In the reading, “could” applies to both “delay” and “raise”. Chanana presents both effects as possibilities if data centre plans face closer checks.

quiz.question: Which statement best captures the main story?

Tech stocks fell as the US midterms added to existing worries about AI.
Worries about AI investment first appeared after the US midterms.

quiz.question: What had Gina Hinojosa promised during her campaign in Texas?
options: To put new data centre construction on hold.
To help new data centres open sooner.
To close data centres that were already operating.
option_feedback: Her promise concerned pausing new construction.
Her promise was to pause new construction.
Her promise concerned new buildings. The brief gives no plan for closing existing centres.

quiz.question: How do the times of the Nasdaq and Nikkei figures in the brief differ?
options: Both figures come from early trading.
The Nasdaq figure comes from early trading, and the Nikkei figure is from the close.
The Nasdaq figure is from the close, and the Nikkei figure comes from early trading.

The brief says the Nasdaq “closed” lower and gives the Nikkei figure for “early trading”.

quiz.question: Why was trading briefly paused in Seoul?

Make it easier to sell tech stocks.

Investors were questioning the value of their investment in AI. The phrase describes whether the investment is worth the money.
If an investment “pays off”, it brings enough financial benefit to be worth making.

quiz.question: What might companies need to plan for, based on Chanana’s comments?
options: Their projects may take longer and cost more.
Closer checks may let them start construction sooner.
They can already tell how much extra each project will cost.
option_feedback: Chanana said closer checks could delay projects and raise costs.

quiz.question: Whose support did Greg Brockman say would take more work to win?
options: Investors in tech companies.
Local communities.
Members of Congress.
option_feedback: Investors appear elsewhere in the brief. Brockman was talking about local communities.
Brockman said more work was needed to win support from local communities.
The brief mentions Congress in connection with the election results. Brockman was talking about local communities.

quiz.question: A town plans to review a building proposal. Which sentence uses “could” and the base form of a verb to describe a possible effect?
options: The review could delays the opening.
The review could to delay the opening.
The review could delay the opening.

vocabulary.definition: A position in which a stock market benchmark or a company’s market value is at least 10% below its recent high.

To limit the intensity or spread of something seen as harmful or excessive.
Specific policy proposals put directly to voters for a decision.
An official pause in an activity, intended to be temporary.
The possibility of a future event that people are taking into account now.

grammar.explanation: An opening clause with “although” acknowledges a point before the main clause qualifies what readers might infer from it. Here, Chanana acknowledges a shared goal, then shows why that goal leaves the pace and cost of expansion open to debate.

The elections signalled that investors expected weaker demand for computer chips.
The elections prompted trading restrictions that drove technology stocks lower.
option_feedback: The brief links the drop to concerns that AI development could slow and discusses those concerns alongside doubts about investment returns.
The concern linked to the elections is the pace of AI development. The brief gives no forecast for chip demand.
The steep drop in the Kospi triggered the trading halt. The brief describes the halt as a response to a decline.

quiz.question: How does the starting point for the Nasdaq’s daily decline of more than 5.5% differ from the starting point used to determine whether it is in “correction territory”?
options: The daily decline is measured from the previous close, while the correction is measured from that day’s opening level.
The daily decline is measured from the recent high, while the correction is measured from the previous close.
The daily decline is measured from the previous close, while the correction is measured from the recent high.
option_feedback: The daily comparison uses the previous close, but the correction is measured from the recent high.
This reverses the two reference points. The recent high is the basis for measuring the correction.
The daily figure compares two closing levels, while the correction measures how far the Nasdaq has moved below its recent high.

quiz.question: What does the phrase “in an effort to curb panic selling” establish about the Kospi trading halt?
options: It establishes that the halt reduced the amount of panic selling.
It identifies the purpose of the halt while leaving its effect open.
It indicates that traders had regained confidence by the time the halt began.
option_feedback: The phrase “in an effort to” introduces an aim. The sentence gives no outcome for the amount of panic selling.
The halt was intended to limit panic selling. Its effectiveness would require separate evidence.
The sentence explains why trading was halted. It does not assess traders’ confidence.

quiz.question: What can readers conclude from the description of the “ballot measures”?
options: Proposals to restrict data centre development were put before voters across the country.
Voters approved the proposed restrictions in most of the places that considered them.
The proposals set out the same rules for data centre construction across the country.
option_feedback: The brief reports that dozens of proposals appeared on ballots across the country and identifies their shared aim.
A place on the ballot establishes that voters could consider a proposal. The brief gives no tally of approvals.
The proposals shared a broad aim. The brief leaves their individual terms unspecified.

quiz.question: What is the most precise interpretation of Gina Hinojosa’s pledge?
options: She pledged a permanent ban on building new data centres.
She pledged a temporary shutdown of operating data centres.
She pledged a temporary halt to the construction of new data centres.
option_feedback: A “moratorium” is intended to be temporary. The pledge concerns a pause in new construction.
The pledge concerns construction of new facilities. Operating existing facilities is a separate activity.
The word “moratorium” conveys a temporary halt, and the brief identifies new construction as its scope.

quiz.question: What does “yield lower returns than they had counted on” suggest about investors’ concern?
options: The investments might produce a net loss, which is the specific risk identified by the phrase.
The investments might generate less financial benefit than investors had expected and relied on.
The cost of building the infrastructure might be lower than investors had anticipated.
option_feedback: A return can fall short of expectations and still be positive. The phrase leaves the actual outcome open.
Here “yield” means “produce”, and “counted on” indicates that investors had relied on receiving the returns they expected.
The comparison concerns the financial benefit investors might receive. It gives no comparison of construction costs.

quiz.question: Which inference about greater “scrutiny” is supported by Chanana’s assessment?
options: The process of examining projects more closely could affect their timelines and costs.
Closer examination would concentrate on electricity bills and leave environmental effects outside the process.
The risk of higher costs arises only if a project is ultimately refused.
option_feedback: Chanana identifies delays and higher costs as possible consequences of closer examination.
Chanana mentions environmental effects alongside electricity bills as matters that could receive closer attention.
Chanana describes a potential rise in costs across the industry. She does not limit that risk to projects that are refused.

quiz.question: What does Chanana’s distinction between backing AI and allowing its infrastructure to expand at any pace or cost imply?
options: Supporting AI depends on keeping construction at its current pace.
Agreement on AI leadership settles how fast projects should go ahead.
Support for AI is compatible with limits on how its infrastructure expands.
option_feedback: Chanana separates the broad goal from decisions about construction. She specifies no preferred pace.
The shared goal is leadership in AI. Chanana leaves decisions about the pace and cost of expansion open.
Chanana presents support for the technology as a position that can coexist with limits on the pace or cost of expansion.

quiz.question: Which sentence uses an opening “although” clause to acknowledge support for AI before qualifying what that support implies?
options: Although a council may oppose a particular data centre, it can still support AI research.
Although a council supports AI research, it may still oppose a particular data centre.
Because a council supports AI research, it may oppose a particular data centre.
option_feedback: This sentence is grammatical. Its opening clause acknowledges possible opposition to the centre, and its main clause makes support for research the central point.
The opening clause acknowledges support for research. The main clause qualifies what that support implies for a specific project.
The conjunction “because” presents support for research as a reason for opposing the centre. The task asks for a concession.

quiz.question: What does “backlash” convey about the response to data centres?
options: It conveys a strong negative reaction to data centres.
It conveys a cautious review of proposed data centre projects.
It conveys a binding decision to block data centre construction.
option_feedback: The word “backlash” signals strong opposition. The sentence separately reports that some technology leaders were surprised by it.
A cautious review is a form of examination. Here “backlash” describes the strength and negative direction of the reaction.
The word describes opposition. Whether that opposition leads to a binding decision is a separate question.

Political parties pursuing US leadership in AI.
Local communities.

The parties’ shared goal appears in a separate part of the brief. Brockman focuses on support at the community level.
Brockman says more work is needed to secure the backing of local communities.
